description: I'm Nada and I'm interested in technology
summary:
Our project is an interactive online Space Museum that explores six pieces of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars: four on the Moon and two on Mars. We developed a website where visitors can discover the history, missions, and locations of these objects through six interactive exhibits, a clickable map, and a historical timeline.

To make learning more engaging and accessible, the website offers both Arabic and English languages, along with an interactive quiz called "Space Challenge." The quiz tests visitors' knowledge through randomly selected questions and provides explanations for incorrect answers, helping them learn while having fun.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming scientific information about forgotten space equipment into an engaging and accessible educational experience. It is important because it raises awareness of space exploration history, highlights the scientific value of these objects, and reminds us that even equipment left behind in space has a story worth discovering.
details: Our project is an interactive online Space Museum that allows visitors to explore six pieces of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars: four on the Moon and two on Mars. The website contains six exhibits where visitors can discover each object's name, mission, location, history, and photographs. It also features an interactive map displaying the locations of all six objects, allowing users to click on each location to explore it. A timeline presents important dates and events related to the missions. Additionally, the website includes Arabic and English language options and a fun interactive quiz called "Space Challenge." The quiz randomly selects 10 questions from a bank of 25 questions. Visitors choose their answers and receive immediate feedback showing whether each answer is correct or incorrect. If an answer is wrong, the quiz explains why and provides the correct information. This makes the quiz both a testing tool and a learning experience. The project aims to make space science more accessible, encourage curiosity, and turn learning into an enjoyable experience. Its intended impact is to raise awareness of space exploration history and highlight the scientific importance of equipment left behind during space missions. We developed the website using HTML, with the assistance of AI tools throughout the development process. We relied exclusively on NASA's official resources for scientific information and photographs. The website is responsive and designed to work on both computers and mobile devices without requiring special hardware. Our creativity comes from combining storytelling, interactive maps, a historical timeline, bilingual content, and gamification into one educational platform. Our team divided responsibilities among its members, with each person responsible for a specific part of the project. Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, ease of navigation, visual design, and user engagement to create an informative and enjoyable experience.
